source.reference: Windows Electron source checkout; M3D20-10 observed runs on 2026-11-11
source.derivation: Ceiling of the highest observed p95 or sampled RSS across baseline, after-worker and final source profiles, plus 20%, rounded up to a practical 50 or 100 unit boundary. These are regression thresholds, not installed release claims.

longMemory.reference: Windows i9-12900K source build, continuous 100-action cycles for at least two hours
longMemory.derivation: The short-run 1500 MiB ceiling plus 548 MiB headroom, with at most 64 MiB late-window growth; renderer-private and GPU-process ceilings are separate native-memory safeguards. The source GPU-process peak was revised from 512 to 544 MiB after three clean 800-switch runs of the same renderer bundle peaked at 445.5, 520.7, and 524.5 MiB while late GPU growth stayed within 32 MiB. The 544 MiB ceiling leaves 19.5 MiB above the highest measured peak. Long-memory receipt v2 applies the same absolute ceilings to all samples and measures late retention from cycle-end post-GC samples. This source budget does not qualify an installed candidate or replace the two-hour soak.

installed.reason: No clean installed 2.0 candidate has been measured on this reference device. Require a package hash, installed-host receipt, repeat runs and a separately frozen budget.
